day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Leonardo Express train (€14) or the cheaper FL1 regional train (~€8) to Roma Termini. Grab a quick late-night snack near the station and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle in and rest for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A – in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night slice of pizza al taglio near Roma Termini (€3–5) – try any of the small pizzerias open late around the station area

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival day light. Validate your train ticket before boarding to avoid fines. Exchange a small amount of cash or use an ATM at the airport for immediate expenses. The FL1 regional train is the most budget-friendly airport transfer option.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a classic Roman breakfast at a local bar near the hotel – espresso and cornetto. Head to the Colosseum area and explore the exterior of the Colosseum (iconic for photos). Purchase a combined ticket (~€16) that covers the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill – valid for 2 consecutive days, making it excellent value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use your combined ticket to walk through the Roman Forum and climb Palatine Hill for sweeping views over ancient Rome. Take your time among the ruins of the Temple of Saturn, the Arch of Titus, and the Imperial Palaces on the hill. This is a 2–3 hour exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit – Stay on Palatine Hill into the golden hour to watch the sun set over the Forum. The warm light on the ancient stones is breathtaking and completely free with your combined ticket. Afterward, stroll to the nearby Testaccio neighborhood for an authentic, budget-friendly Roman dinner.

meals.breakfast: Espresso + cornetto at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed panino from a nearby alimentari (deli) or a street food stall near the Colosseum – avoid tourist trap restaurants in the immediate Colosseum area (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Trattoria in Testaccio neighborhood – try cacio e pepe or coda alla vaccinara. Look for a 'menu turistico' (set menu) for €12–15 including primo, secondo, and house wine

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum tickets online in advance to avoid long queues. Bring a refillable water bottle – Rome has free drinking fountains (nasoni) throughout the city. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone walking.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Book the first entry slot (8:00 AM) online in advance to beat the crowds. Explore one of the world's greatest art collections: the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Budget 2–3 hours. Ticket ~€17 (standard online booking).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican Museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica – entry is FREE. Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot). Spend time in St. Peter's Square and explore the grandeur of the Basilica's interior, including Michelangelo's Pietà.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the charming Prati neighborhood near the Vatican for an affordable dinner. Then take a leisurely evening stroll across the Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge to admire Castel Sant'Angelo lit up at night – free to view from the outside and stunning.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick espresso and pastry at a bar near the Vatican before your museum entry (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Sandwich or supplì (fried rice balls) from a local bar in Prati neighborhood – avoid restaurants immediately outside the Vatican (€6–9)
meals.dinner: Casual trattoria in Prati – look for daily specials (piatti del giorno) which are typically cheaper. Try pasta all'amatriciana (€10–14 for a full meal)

day_by_day.notes: The Vatican dress code requires covered shoulders and knees – bring a scarf or light layer. Pre-booking Vatican tickets is essential; same-day entry is nearly impossible without a reservation. The Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except the last Sunday of each month when entry is free but extremely crowded).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic centro storico on foot. Start at the Pantheon (free entry or small fee if applicable by 2027 – check in advance). Marvel at the 2,000-year-old perfectly preserved dome. Then walk to nearby Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers – completely free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Campo de' Fiori market (open until ~2:00 PM) for fresh produce, local cheeses, and cheap street food. Pick up ingredients for a self-catered snack. Afterward, explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood and walk along the Tiber River. Visit the free exterior of the Teatro di Marcello (Rome's older 'Colosseum').
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere neighborhood dinner – one of Rome's most atmospheric and authentic areas. Explore the winding medieval streets, visit the beautiful Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica (free), and enjoy dinner at one of the many budget-friendly local osterias.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a bar near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Self-assembled picnic from Campo de' Fiori market – bread, cheese, olives, and seasonal fruit (€6–8 total)
meals.dinner: Osteria in Trastevere – look for restaurants away from the main piazza for better prices. Try spaghetti cacio e pepe or tonnarelli. Budget €12–16 for a full meal with house wine

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon may have an entry fee by 2027 – check the official website before visiting. Trastevere gets busy in the evenings; arrive before 7:30 PM for easier seating. Many of Rome's best experiences (piazzas, basilicas, neighborhoods) are completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery – one of Rome's finest art museums housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings. Entry is ~€15 but MUST be booked in advance as visits are timed (2-hour slots). Arrive early for the first slot. The gallery is set within the beautiful Villa Borghese park.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, spend time in the vast Villa Borghese park – completely free. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€3–5), stroll through the gardens, or simply relax. Walk up to the Pincian Hill terrace (Terrazza del Pincio) for one of the best free panoramic views over Rome and Piazza del Popolo.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Piazza del Popolo – a grand piazza with twin baroque churches and an ancient Egyptian obelisk (free to visit). Explore the upscale but walkable Piazza di Spagna area and the Spanish Steps at dusk. Note: eating and drinking on the Spanish Steps is prohibited. Find a nearby wine bar (enoteca) for an affordable aperitivo.

meals.breakfast: Bar breakfast near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park – grab supplies from a nearby alimentari or supermarket (€6–8). Eating in the park is a quintessential Roman experience.
meals.dinner: Aperitivo hour at a local enoteca near Piazza del Popolo (some offer free snacks with a drink purchase, €5–8 per drink). Follow with a simple trattoria dinner (€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance – book as early as possible. The park is a wonderful free resource for relaxation mid-trip. Look for 'happy hour' or aperitivo deals between 6–9 PM at bars throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Capitoline Museums (€15) – the world's oldest public museums, sitting atop Capitoline Hill. See the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf sculpture, and incredible views of the Roman Forum from the terrace (a free vantage point if you skip the museum). Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Circus Maximus (free to visit the grounds) – the ancient chariot racing track that once held 250,000 spectators. Continue to the Aventine Hill neighborhood to find the famous Knights of Malta keyhole (Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta) – a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome through a keyhole, completely free. Nearby, visit the beautiful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for more panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Trevi Fountain at dusk (free) – toss a coin and make a wish. The fountain is magical in the evening light. Explore the surrounding streets for a gelato from a reputable gelateria (look for 'artigianale' signs). Have a final dinner in the lively Monti neighborhood – Rome's hippest yet still affordable bohemian quarter.

meals.breakfast: Bar breakfast near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pizza al taglio (pizza by the slice) from a local bakery in the Testaccio or Aventine area (€4–7) – this is authentic Roman fast food
meals.dinner: Dinner in Monti neighborhood – excellent trattorias and wine bars. Try a local osteria for pasta and a carafe of house wine (€13–17)

day_by_day.notes: The Trevi Fountain area is very crowded on weekends – visit in the evening for a slightly better experience. Monti is walkable from the Colosseum area and has excellent budget dining. Gelato tip: avoid places with mountains of brightly colored gelato – true artisan gelato is stored in covered metal containers.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Rome – visit the Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (open Sunday mornings until ~2:00 PM). One of Rome's largest and most famous markets, great for unique souvenirs, vintage finds, and local atmosphere. Browse for affordable mementos to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final stroll through Rome's streets – revisit any favorite spots or piazzas you want to see one last time. Visit any free basilicas you haven't seen yet, such as Santa Maria Maggiore or San Giovanni in Laterano (both free and architecturally stunning). Pick up any last souvenirs from the market or local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the week, or try something new in the Pigneto neighborhood (Rome's up-and-coming area, very budget-friendly and authentic). Pack bags and prepare for departure. Depending on your return flight, arrange transport back to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast – treat yourself to a sit-down breakfast at a slightly nicer bar (€5–8) or enjoy a cornetto and cappuccino at a classic Roman bar one last time (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Street food at Porta Portese market or a quick pizza al taglio nearby (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner – splurge slightly on your last night. A good trattoria with a full meal including antipasto, pasta, main, and wine for €20–25 per person is still very reasonable by European standards

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese market is cash-only – bring euros. For airport transport on departure, the FL1 regional train from Roma Ostiense or Trastevere station is cheaper than the Leonardo Express (€8 vs €14). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Overall weekly budget estimate: accommodation aside, daily expenses of €40–60 per person (transport, entry fees, meals) are achievable with careful planning.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train or a pre-booked private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Grab a light snack from the hotel bar or a nearby 24-hour convenience store if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack at the hotel bar upon arrival — try a panino or bruschetta if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm your hotel transfer in advance. Exchange some cash or use an ATM at the airport for tips and small purchases. Rome taxis from Fiumicino to the city center have a fixed rate of approximately €50.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely Italian breakfast at a nearby café — espresso, cornetto, and fresh orange juice. Take a gentle orientation stroll around your neighborhood to get your bearings and soak in the Roman atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the iconic Trevi Fountain, Spanish Steps, and the Pantheon for a self-guided walking tour of central Rome. These landmarks are close together and perfect for a relaxed first full afternoon. Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain and admire the Baroque grandeur of the Pantheon (entry fee applies).
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the Piazza Navona area for aperitivo hour. Enjoy a Aperol Spritz or Negroni at an outdoor café. Stroll the piazza and watch street artists perform before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Sant'Eustachio or a local bar near the hotel — espresso and cornetto (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Grab a classic Roman supplì and pizza al taglio at a local forno (bakery) near the Pantheon (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Osteria del Pegno near Piazza Navona — mid-range Roman trattoria with cacio e pepe and saltimbocca (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Book the Pantheon entry online in advance to avoid queues. Stay hydrated — Rome in June can be warm. Piazza Navona is lively in the evening and free to enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Book an early morning timed-entry slot (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections, including the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Don't miss St. Peter's Basilica right next door (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Tiber and explore the charming Prati neighborhood near the Vatican. Browse local shops along Via Cola di Rienzo. Rest your feet at a café before heading toward Castel Sant'Angelo for exterior photos and optional interior visit.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join a guided evening food walk through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere, sampling local Roman cuisine including supplì, artichokes, pecorino, and local wines. A perfect immersive introduction to Roman food culture.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near the hotel before the early Vatican start — espresso and pastry (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pizzarium Bonci in Prati — Rome's most celebrated pizza al taglio spot (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience — supplementary drinks available for purchase

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Vatican Museums tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in summer. Dress code applies: covered shoulders and knees required for the Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Basilica. The evening food walk typically lasts 3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Cooking Class — Start at Rome's most authentic food market where locals shop daily. Browse stalls of fresh produce, cured meats, cheeses, and Roman street food. Then join a hands-on cooking class where you'll learn to make classic Roman dishes like pasta carbonara, cacio e pepe, or Roman-style artichokes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood on foot — visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (where Keats is buried), admire the Pyramid of Cestius, and browse the vibrant street art in the Ostiense district nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Campo de' Fiori square for aperitivo. Explore the surrounding streets and enjoy a relaxed dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market visit — grab a coffee at a local bar (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared in the cooking class — typically included in the experience
meals.dinner: Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina near Campo de' Fiori — celebrated Roman deli-restaurant with excellent pasta and wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market & Cooking Class is a half-day experience — book in advance. Testaccio is considered the culinary heart of Rome and is very walkable. The cooking class is a highlight for food lovers and typically includes wine.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Private Art Tour — Discover Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside this intimate Baroque villa. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 2 hours, making it one of Rome's most exclusive museum experiences. The private tour adds deep context to the masterpieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's green lung. Rent a rowboat on the lake, stroll through the park, or visit the Pincio Terrace for one of the best panoramic views of Rome's rooftops and domes.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the elegant Parioli or Flaminio neighborhood for a sophisticated dinner. Alternatively, return to the centro storico for a twilight walk along the Tiber River embankment.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel or a pasticceria — cappuccino and brioche (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up supplies from a nearby deli or alimentari (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Il Sorpasso in Prati — stylish Roman bistro with natural wines and seasonal Roman dishes (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery requires advance booking — it often sells out weeks in advance. Only 360 visitors are admitted every 2 hours. The private tour enhances the experience significantly. Villa Borghese is free to enter and ideal for an afternoon recharge.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the ancient Colosseum and surrounding area. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance. Spend the morning marveling at the world's largest ancient amphitheater and learning about gladiatorial history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit — Walk through the ancient ruins of the Roman Forum and climb Palatine Hill as the golden hour light bathes the ruins in warm tones. The combined ticket covers the Colosseum, Forum, and Palatine Hill. Take your time wandering the Via Sacra and imagining ancient Roman life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Aventine Hill neighborhood — visit the famous Knights of Malta keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome, then stroll down to the vibrant Testaccio for a final indulgent dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby bar near the Colosseum area (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a trattoria near the Roman Forum — try rigatoni all'amatriciana (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — beloved Roman trattoria carved into Monte dei Cocci with exceptional cacio e pepe and tiramisu (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The combined Colosseum + Forum + Palatine Hill ticket is valid for one day. Arrive at the Colosseum early morning to avoid peak heat and crowds. Bring water and sun protection — the Forum and Palatine Hill are largely unshaded. The sunset from Palatine Hill is spectacular in June.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final slow Roman breakfast at a beloved local café. Take a last morning stroll through your favorite neighborhood or revisit a piazza you loved. Pick up souvenirs — quality olive oil, pasta, or local ceramics from a deli or specialty food shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final gelato at a top gelateria (try Fatamorgana for artisan flavors or Giolitti for a classic experience). Head to the airport via Leonardo Express or private transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome — carry the flavors, art, and memories of the Eternal City with you.

meals.breakfast: Final espresso and cornetto at a classic Roman bar — savor the ritual one last time (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before checkout — a slice of pizza al taglio or a tramezzino sandwich (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Fiumicino. The Leonardo Express runs every 30 minutes from Roma Termini and takes 32 minutes to the airport. Confirm hotel checkout time the evening before. Consider buying vacuum-packed Roman pecorino or guanciale at the airport duty-free as edible souvenirs.

meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — burrata with heirloom tomatoes, grilled branzino, and a chilled glass of Vermentino

day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — wander the cobblestone streets of Rome's most atmospheric neighborhood sampling supplì al telefono, cacio e pepe, artichokes alla giudia, and local Lazio wines poured by passionate local producers and trattoria owners.

day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the lunch you cooked with your chef and fellow participants. Afterwards, explore the Testaccio neighborhood on foot — visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (resting place of Keats and Shelley) and the contemporary MACRO Testaccio art space.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset cocktails on the beachfront terrace. Optional: private in-resort dinner under the stars with a personalized menu curated by the executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — eggs any style, seasonal fruit platter, warm pastries, and a selection of Italian cold cuts and cheeses
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during the Testaccio cooking class form a celebratory sit-down lunch with wine pairings selected by the chef-instructor
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort — request a customized tasting menu with a focus on Roman and coastal Lazio cuisine; sommelier-selected wine pairing with each course

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM including the market visit and lunch. Book at least 2 weeks in advance as classes fill quickly. Wear comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes for the kitchen.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums, housing Marcus Aurelius's original bronze equestrian statue, Caravaggio's St. John the Baptist, and sweeping panoramic views over the Roman Forum from the terrace. The private format allows deep engagement with each masterwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit — descend from the Capitoline into the Forum and walk among the ancient temples, triumphal arches, and sacred roads of the ancient city. Climb Palatine Hill as the afternoon golden light bathes the ruins in amber — one of Rome's most cinematic experiences. A private guide provides historical context that transforms ruins into living history.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo at a rooftop bar with Forum views such as the Terrazza Caffarelli or the rooftop of Hotel Senato. Dinner at a celebrated Roman restaurant in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — avocado toast with bottarga, freshly baked cornetti, a selection of seasonal Italian jams, and a doppio espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Campidoglio area at Caffè Capitolino — light Roman dishes including tonnarelli cacio e pepe, seasonal vegetable antipasti, and a glass of chilled Frascati
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pipero Roma (Corso Vittorio Emanuele II) — a celebrated fine-dining destination with inventive takes on Roman classics; sommelier-guided wine pairing with natural and biodynamic Italian wines

day_by_day.notes: The Palatine Hill and Roman Forum use a combined ticket — include this with the Colosseum ticket for the best value. Sunset visits in June offer light until approximately 8:30 PM, making the golden-hour experience exceptional. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning at leisure — sleep in, enjoy a spa treatment at the resort, or take a private yoga session on the beachfront arranged through the concierge. Optional: visit a high-end gallery in Rome's contemporary art district (Prati or Pigneto) for those wanting more art immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private shopping experience in Rome's luxury quarter — Via Condotti, Via Borgognona, and Piazza di Spagna. Visit flagship stores of Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi (whose headquarters occupy the Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana), and artisan leather goods ateliers. A personal shopping consultant can be arranged through the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve cocktails at the Hassler Hotel's rooftop bar (Imàgo) overlooking the Spanish Steps and Roman skyline — one of the most iconic views in the city. Follow with a grand final dinner at Imàgo restaurant, a Michelin-starred venue with floor-to-ceiling windows and an exceptional cellar.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast in bed — eggs Florentine, smoked salmon, a charcuterie selection, freshly squeezed juices, and a pot of Italian press coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Nino (Via Borgognona) — a Florentine-Roman institution beloved by locals and discerning visitors; ribollita, bistecca, and a bottle of Chianti Classico Riserva
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner at Imàgo at the Hassler Hotel — seven courses showcasing the finest Italian seasonal ingredients with panoramic views of Rome; full wine pairing with sommelier guidance

day_by_day.notes: Reserve Imàgo well in advance — it is one of Rome's most sought-after tables. The Hassler rooftop bar opens at 6:00 PM and gets busy quickly; arrive early for the best window seats. Personal shopping appointments on Via Condotti should be arranged 24–48 hours ahead through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a last walk along the beachfront at sunrise. Pack and check out — the concierge can arrange luggage storage if your flight departs in the evening, allowing a final few hours in the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional final afternoon activity: a private guided walk through Campo de' Fiori and the Jewish Ghetto — Rome's oldest and most layered neighborhood — visiting the Great Synagogue and the ancient Portico d'Ottavia ruins. Stop at a historic pasticceria for a final supplì and espresso standing at the bar, Roman-style.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to Fiumicino Airport. Depart Rome with a curated selection of gourmet souvenirs arranged by the concierge: a bottle of aged Barolo, artisan pasta from Roscioli, and handmade chocolates from Said.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a full spread of Italian pastries, seasonal fruit, cold cuts, cheeses, and a farewell Bellini (prosecco and white peach purée) as a send-off from the team
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Jewish Ghetto at Nonna Betta or Ba'Ghetto — Roman-Jewish cuisine featuring carciofi alla giudia, filetti di baccalà, and ricotta e visciole tart, paired with a glass of local white wine
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Fiumicino's premium lounge or a light meal before boarding — alternatively, the hotel can prepare a gourmet picnic box for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security at Fiumicino. The concierge should arrange the airport transfer 30 minutes earlier than usual given June summer travel volumes. Request a late check-out (subject to availability) to maximize the final morning at the resort.
